name: sad8x8
description: An 8x8 SAD block matcher for motion estimation that computes all 64 absolute pixel differences in parallel and sums them in an adder tree to a 14-bit SAD.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable 8x8 sum-of-absolute-differences (SAD) block matcher for motion estimation. Two NxN pixel blocks (current and reference) are presented as packed buses, with pixel k located at bit position [k*PW+:PW]. All 64 absolute differences |a-b| are computed in parallel and reduced through an adder tree to a single SAD value (max 16320, 14-bit). The block has registered I/O with a single-cycle latency from valid_in to valid_out, and uses no multiply and no memory. It shares the clk/rst/valid/8-bit-pixel conventions of the streaming 3x3 filters and acts as a measurement (reduction) block at the tail of an image pipeline. Parameters are N (block size, default 8) and PW (pixel width, default 8).
key_decisions: Model the 64 absolute-difference cells with generate (one combinational subtract/compare/select unit per pixel) plus an explicit adder-tree reduction, rather than a single large unrolled procedural loop.
Use a 63-adder binary reduction tree for the summation to keep the critical path logarithmic in the number of pixels.
Register both inputs and output so valid_in maps to valid_out with a fixed single-cycle latency, matching the streaming-filter conventions.
Pack both blocks as N*N*PW buses with pixel k at [k*PW+:PW] so the interface is parametric and tool-portable.
Compute absolute difference with subtract/compare/select (no multiply) and keep the design memoryless, so it maps to LUTs/FFs with 0 DSP and 0 BRAM.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: Block-matching motion estimation, sum-of-absolute-differences (SAD) metric (MPEG / H.26x video coding standards).
Systolic/parallel SAD arrays for VLSI motion estimation (e.g. Vos & Stegherr; standard motion-estimation accelerator designs).
